examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: A recognizer must accept every member but may loop on a nonmember. A decider must halt on every input and accept exactly the members. For recognizable-language intersection, dovetail recognizers so one nonterminating run cannot prevent progress of another. A bounded simulation is finite and can be used in reductions or enumerations.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A machine accepts 3 of 8 given inputs, rejects 4, and loops on 1. How many inputs does it halt on?

**Answer: 7.** Acceptance and rejection are both halting outcomes, so it halts on 3+4=7 inputs. Because one input loops, this behaviour cannot be a decider on a domain containing all eight inputs.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
A machine halting on every input need not decide a particular named language unless its acceptance and rejection sets also match that language.

Not accepting is not the same as rejecting when nontermination is possible.
